Subject: QBR prep: contingency & renewal triage — Stratus (Renewal Oct '27)

Team,

We have Stratus' QBR prep next week and I want to lock the internal slate for exec attention and renewal triage. Renewal window is Oct 1 — primary concern is a potential 20% seat-reduction ask tied to their forecasted spend constraints. Elena looped in on visibility.

Immediate asks (please return by EOD Mon):
- Mina: refresh the Risk Register with current usage/latency incidents and the top 3 product gaps they flagged in the last 90 days.
- Neha: confirm contract start/stop dates + any outstanding procurement redlines Proc has surfaced.
- Lauren: draft a 2-slide exec brief (1x account health, 1x proposed mitigation + ask).

Target outputs for the QBR packet:
- Customer Health Snapshot (single page)
- Renewal Risk Register (spreadsheet, ranked)
- Exec Ask + Contingency Plan (what we offer if they request seat reduction: credits, dedicated cadences, pilot pricing)

I'll coordinate a brief with Jordan for exec escalation path if we land in a high-risk lane. CCing Elena so we stay transparent on next steps.

Thanks — Marcus

Subject: Re: QBR prep: contingency & renewal triage — Stratus (Renewal Oct '27)

Marcus / team,

Attached is v3 of the risk register (tabbed: summary / incidents / mitigation). Quick highlights:

- Health score: 62/100 (down 8 pts since last quarter) — driven by sustained latency for long-context batches and a spike in error rates during a March migration.
- Top 3 customer pain points (from CS & telemetry):
  1) Intermittent 5-10s tail latency on 8k+ token sessions (impacts product demo and internal adoption)
  2) Confusion on token accounting during streaming sessions (billing queries)
  3) Limited visibility into model variant fallbacks during outages (they'd like a deterministic SLA behavior)
- Recent incidents (last 90d): 3 P1-ish spikes (Mar 18 migration bump; Apr 6 region failover delay; May 29 degraded kv-cache for specific model family).

Proposed mitigations and immediate offers:
- Offer 90-day dedicated pilot (no-fee credits for first 6 weeks) + a joint playbook for long-context optimizations.
- Short-term: enable extra tracing hooks and a token accounting audit (1-week delivery).
- If they insist on a seat reduction, propose a staged rollback: 10% credits + 30-day performance SLA and a second review before further reductions.

I've flagged two rows as 'exec attention' (rows 4 and 7) where they expect contract concessions. See notes column for recommended ask.

I attached the snapshot PDF for the one-pager; please review and call out any numbers that look off.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Customer_Health_Snapshot_Stratus.pdf (1 page)]

From: Elena Torres <elena@stratus.ai>

Cc: procure@stratus.ai
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 08:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: QBR prep: contingency & renewal triage — Stratus (Renewal Oct '27)

Marcus / Mina,

Thanks for the early visibility and the snapshot — that was helpful. Two quick clarifications from our side:
- The latency impact is customer-visible for our analytics team; if you can offer a short-term SLA credit while you remediate, that will help us keep internal buy-in.
- Procurement is asking for clarity on auto-scaling guarantees and a contact for escalation during region failovers.

On the renewal, we are not looking to exit but are evaluating seat counts across teams. If we can secure a short-term deal to protect costs while you deliver the pilot and the trace accounting, we can likely hold to a smaller reduction.

Can we get the exec brief and a concise list of asks by tomorrow (Wed EOD PST)?

— Elena
Elena Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, Stratus

Subject: Fwd: QBR prep: contingency & renewal triage — Stratus (Renewal Oct '27)

Jordan / Lauren — forwarding the thread and attachments. TL;DR: Stratus is evaluating seat counts; main risk drivers are latency (long-context) and billing transparency asks. They want the exec brief + explicit asks by Wed EOD PST.

My recommended exec attention items (for your review):
- Approve a 6-week pilot (dedicated capacity) with a 90-day check-in and 10% credit if SLAs missed in that window.
- Commit to a prioritized engineering slot for the token-accounting audit (target 7 business days).
- Prepare an escalation contact list and a measurable region-failover SLA addendum to the renewal term sheet.

If approved, I'll present this as our official contingency and ask for the QBR. If not approved, we'll pivot to a conservative credit-only offer and escalate to VP.
